traits.note: Watson and Dallwitz, The Families of Flowering Plants (DELTA data, items edited May 2026), family Stemonuraceae: leaves alternate; leaves simple; margins entire, crenate, serrate or dentate; veins usually pinnate, rarely palmate; leaves evergreen; stipules absent; plants monoecious, polygamous or dioecious; ovary superior; floral cup absent; stems woody; flowers in cymes or in racemes; flowers actinomorphic; perianth sepals and petals; fruit drupe; parts of each whorl (4-) 5 (-7); stamens 4 to 5 (-7); carpels 2. Read from the coded states by script (spec-rework/b1/delta/mapdelta.py); a state the authors qualify (rarely, usually, a share) keeps its word, an unqualified one beside a usual state reads as sometimes.
